_comment: Remote control for OpenBat: kill switches (see OpenBat/FeatureFlags.swift), two messages, and default VALUES (see OpenBat/RemoteDefaults.swift). Edit this file on `main` — the branch FeatureFlagStore.remoteURL names — or nothing happens; the copy on a version branch is only source. Leave features true while a build is in review; flip after approval and before release.
_comment_features: Only `false` does anything: every flag is compiled ON, and this file can only override a default to off. Setting one back to true (or removing it) returns the app to the state Apple reviewed. `configMenu` locks the config menu itself: false closes the menu, drops every local override it had set, and returns the iNaturalist posting-cap bypass to its compiled state.
_comment_maintenance: Interrupts. Shown as an alert once per distinct message, and standing in Settings while set. For explaining that part of the app is switched off. Needs `maintenance: true` as well as text.
_comment_notice: Does not interrupt. A standing note at the top of Settings for as long as this is non-empty — a known issue, a release note, a thank-you. No alert, no once-per-message bookkeeping. Empty string is off.
_comment_defaults: Default VALUES. Only the keys listed in `Tunable` (RemoteDefaults.swift) exist; anything else is ignored, and so is any value outside that parameter's declared range — a rejected value is ignored, never clamped, so a typo fails visibly rather than half-applying in the field. Two rules worth knowing before editing: (1) these move a default, not a user's choice — anyone who has moved the matching slider keeps their own value, and only untouched installs follow this file; (2) a change takes effect at the NEXT launch, because the file arrives a moment after the app has built its settings. Per-model AutoID values are deliberately NOT settable here: they decide what a recording is identified as, and belong to a build. Delete a key to return that parameter to its compiled default.
_comment_available: Every parameter that can be set, with the value the app ships with and the range it will accept. Reference only — this key is ignored by the app, and listing a parameter here does NOT set it. To change one, copy its name into `defaults` below with a number. To put it back, delete it from `defaults` again. The values quoted here are those of the build in review as of 2026-09-09; the app is the authority, and `Tunable` in RemoteDefaults.swift is where both the list and the ranges actually live.
